SULAMI:v2p374#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p374#2/r1.speaker: ابن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p374#2/r1.claim: At resurrection a person flees after recognizing his helplessness and turns toward the one who can remove distress; if recognized in this life, he would rely only on God and rest in trust and surrender.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r1.claim: The crisis is so grave that a person pays no attention to even the closest relatives.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r2.claim: Flight here is not physical running away; it means abandoning a brother's loyalty or avoiding his questions out of preoccupation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r4.claim: Flight can also mean refusing to support one's relatives, since no patron will help another on that day.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p237/r5.claim: Another sense is avoiding questioning by relatives, supported by the statement that no close friend will ask another.

JISHUMI:v10p7292/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r1.claim: The man flees from his wife and nearest family because he is wholly occupied with himself and cannot attend to them.

JISHUMI:v10p7292/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r2.claim: One explanation is that he fears their claims against him for debts and injustices between them.

JISHUMI:v10p7292/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r3.claim: Another explanation is that he knows they cannot help him or one another; the wording does not require literal flight, only disregard and inability to benefit each other.

JISHUMI:v10p7292/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r4.claim: A believer may flee relatives who belong to the people of Hell and become their enemy.

JISHUMI:v10p7292/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r5.claim: Another explanation says people turn from family toward the only one able to remove distress, as they would turn to God if this were manifest in worldly life.

JISHUMI:v10p7292/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r6.claim: He may flee to avoid seeing the humiliation that befalls them.

JISHUMI:v10p7292/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r7.claim: Another explanation attributes the flight to distress at the magnitude of what has happened.

JISHUMI:v10p7292/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r8.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7292/r8.claim: He reports that Abraham flees his father, Muhammad his father, Noah his father, Abel his brother, and Lot his wife, then recited this verse.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p339#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p339#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p339#2/r3.claim: Each person flees close relatives, too occupied with their own fate to turn toward anyone.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p339#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p339#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p339#2/r4.claim: Qatada gives examples: Abel from Cain, Muhammad from his mother, Abraham from his father, Lot from his wife, and Noah from his son.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r2.claim: The relatives are listed in descending order of affection and tenderness, although these are normally the people one would not abandon in hardship.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r3.speaker: أبو أناس جوية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r3.claim: Abu Anas Juwayya reads the hāʾ in أخيه وأمه وأبيه with ḍamma.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r4.speaker: منذر بن سعيد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r4.claim: Mundhir ibn Saʿid and others say each person flees to avoid being pursued for claims and obligations created by past dealings.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r5.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r5.claim: Most interpreters explain the flight as caused by the terror of the day, like the prophets saying each thinks only of himself.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r8.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p440#2/r8.claim: The Prophet told Aisha that it would not matter at the Resurrection whether she was clothed, then recited this passage; he said something similar to Sawda when they feared people would see one another.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:26-36/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:26-36/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:26-36/r7.claim: At the blast, people flee relatives because they are absorbed in themselves and know they cannot help, or fear claims for neglected rights; the order from brother to parents, spouse, and children intensifies the effect.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#14/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#14/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#14/r1.claim: A person flees his brother, mother, and father because of claims owed between them or because he is occupied with himself.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Deafening Blast is a name for Resurrection, magnified by God as a warning; Ibn Jarir suggests it may name the trumpet blast itself.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r2.speaker: البغوي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r2.claim: Al-Baghawi says the term means the cry of Resurrection because it strikes the ears so forcefully it nearly deafens them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r3.claim: People will see their relatives yet flee from them because the terror and ordeal are so great.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r4.claim: Ikrima describes spouses and children refusing even one good deed requested by a relative at Judgment, fearing they need their own deeds to escape.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r5.claim: In the authentic intercession report, the resolute messengers each say “myself”; even Jesus asks only for himself, not Mary, his mother.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p325#2/r6.claim: Qatada says people flee from those they love most and from their closest relatives because of the terror of that Day.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p333/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p333/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p333/r1.claim: Although a wife is the closest companion and most deeply attached to the heart, a person would defend her in hardship.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p48#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p48#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p48#3/r1.claim: On the Day of Resurrection a person turns away from his brother, mother, father, wife, and children, neither accompanying them nor asking after them as in worldly life, because he is absorbed in his own fate.

ELMALILI:80:3-42#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42#6/r4.claim: The list moves upward through degrees of kinship and love, showing that a person will flee even from the closest and dearest relatives on that day.

ELMALILI:80:3-42#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42#6/r6.claim: Relatives may demand an account: a brother for lack of help, parents for neglect, a wife for unlawful provision, and children for failure to teach religion.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r1.claim: The preposition min can mark the cause of fleeing, as in fleeing from a lion, or mean separation, like an; both readings fit the passage.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r2.claim: Fleeing from one's closest relatives reveals the day's terror: people imagine flight from those undergoing punishment may save them, though they know they share their deeds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r3.claim: The sequence climbs in closeness: brotherhood begins in childhood, parents are closer, the mother is named first for stronger attachment and rhyme, then spouse and children form the household.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r4.claim: Listing each relative instead of saying ‘nearest kin’ vividly brings the terror before the listener.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p135/r6.claim: The more plausible reading is a believer fleeing disbelieving relatives to avoid being held accountable for their persistence in unbelief.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r1.claim: The preposition min can mark the cause of fleeing, as in fleeing from a lion, or mean separation, like an; both readings fit the passage.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r2.claim: Fleeing from one's closest relatives reveals the day's terror: people imagine flight from those undergoing punishment may save them, though they know they share their deeds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r3.claim: The sequence climbs in closeness: brotherhood begins in childhood, parents are closer, the mother is named first for stronger attachment and rhyme, then spouse and children form the household.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r4.claim: Listing each relative instead of saying ‘nearest kin’ vividly brings the terror before the listener.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#32/r6.claim: The more plausible reading is a believer fleeing disbelieving relatives to avoid being held accountable for their persistence in unbelief.

TABATABAI:80:25-36/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:25-36/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:25-36/r10.claim: People flee their closest family because the overwhelming crisis absorbs all attention, leaving no capacity to care about anyone else.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r1.claim: Even close kin cannot draw attention on that day; a brother will not heed his brother’s pleas.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r2.claim: No one will have the courage to share hardships even with his wife and sons.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r3.claim: The day's terror will make everyone care only for himself: relatives will not heed pleas or share one another's hardships.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p191/r4.claim: Sūrah al-Maʿārij describes the same estrangement and ransom offered by the sinner, but reverses the order of relatives: here distant-to-near, there near-to-distant.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r1.claim: The closing scene of Resurrection shakes anyone able to reflect on life's meaning, value, purpose, and outcome beyond transient pleasures and anxieties.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r3.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r3.claim: One explanation for fleeing relatives is that the terror leaves everyone consumed by their own danger, unable to think of others.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r4.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r4.claim: People may flee relatives because they fear them demanding the rights owed through kinship.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r5.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r5.claim: A person may flee so relatives will not see the distressing condition he is in.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r6.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r6.claim: A person may flee because he cannot help suffering relatives or prevent what befalls them.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:33/r7.claim: Al-Naziat 79:8–9 describes hearts almost leaping from fear and eyes covered by terror at the gathering.
